what: ATTN-RATE (2026-10-22): the attention's own rate after INFER-ATTN, every value as it was -- EXP-LANES (the BCIR exponential's loops a step at a time over a block of elements, so several vectors' polynomial chains are in flight under any compiler; clang's interleave pragma on the SiLU and SwiGLU loops) and CTX-WIDTH (the AVX-512 context's 48-channel block run as the 16-lane vectors its channels reach) -- measured on the committed tree against the tree before it: the cross-build hashes, the kernels with both builds in one process, the attention's phases, the decoder's forward and training step, and the GEO study's attention model built as the study builds it.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 4 vCPUs (family 6, model 85: AVX-512F and VNNI, no AMX); Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1) and gcc 13.3.0; Python 3.11.15, NumPy 2.2.6, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Before: 97bcba1d2c66a46c92b7620d1b08b931f1b6280e (bcir_tensor.c 760f4c82f7975047...); after: a provisional commit of this change, b4450745420391477175fa3aa6447826e98c8781 (bcir_tensor.c 0e76ef6b44701100...), with nothing uncommitted at either end. Wall times are indicative: one virtualized host, one process at a time; the kernels and the training step compare both builds inside one process (each round's outputs equal across the arms first), the forward in rotated processes, each beside an A/A control.
